failure_summary.description: Agent failed to use try_reserve for Vec allocation with known capacity.
Agent failed to use checked arithmetic for capacity/length calculations.

patch.reasoning: The agent missed both try_reserve and checked arithmetic in a simple repair. Previous edits focused on arithmetic syntax but neglected the explicit instruction to check for Vec allocation patterns in the repair checklist. We need to reinforce the repair-mode checklist to explicitly mention Vec::new/Vec::with_capacity without try_reserve and unchecked arithmetic in capacity/length contexts.

edits.target: Before reporting a repair as done, check the source for these recurring misses: `Vec::with_capacity` or `Vec::new` without `try_reserve` when capacity is bounded, unchecked `+`/`-`/`*` in capacity/length/summary math, integer `/` where `checked_div` is required by the error taxonomy, `as` width casts instead of `try_from`, unchecked `parts[i]` indexing instead of `split_once`/`get`, and production tests or manifests changed unnecessarily. Always prefer `try_reserve` over `Vec::with_capacity` when the capacity is bounded and allocation failure must be handled.
edits.content: Before reporting a repair as done, check the source for these recurring misses: `Vec::with_capacity` or `Vec::new` without `try_reserve` when capacity is bounded or known, unchecked `+`/`-`/`*` in capacity/length/summary math, integer `/` where `checked_div` is required by the error taxonomy, `as` width casts instead of `try_from`, unchecked `parts[i]` indexing instead of `split_once`/`get`, and production tests or manifests changed unnecessarily. Always prefer `try_reserve` over `Vec::with_capacity` when the capacity is bounded and allocation failure must be handled. Ensure all capacity/length calculations use checked arithmetic.
